title: Rolling Refund Limits and Customer Limit-Review Claims — Cartwise Grocery Orders
content:
On Cartwise Grocery Orders, item refunds for missing, damaged, wrong-item and quality issues are weighed across all of a customer's orders against rolling limits, and an issue that would cross them goes to the refund review team as the customer's own limit-review claim.

## Rolling limits and the limit-review claim

1. The agent books a new `missing`, `damaged`, `wrong_item` or `quality` refund only while the customer's count of such refunds across all of their orders, dated within the rolling 90 calendar days ending today, is below the rolling refund-count limit and their amount in that window plus the amount now asked does not exceed the rolling refund-amount limit, both taken from the service level of the order concerned.
2. When either limit would be crossed, nothing is booked by the agent and no part of the issue is registered as an over-cap request; the customer submits the whole issue as their own limit-review claim with request_type `refund_limit_review`, asking for the limit-review claim amount this rule computes, and the review team decides it.
3. This rule prices a limit-review claim on a perishable line that was handed over as ordered (no substitution and no not-found decision on it).
4. A limit-review claim is weighed against the rolling limits only after the refund of every line billed although recorded as not found stands on the order.
5. A limit-review claim is registered only once the part of every line recorded as not found that lies above its unfound-line room stands as a submitted over-cap review request.

## Reading the limits

- **Count test.** The customer's missing, damaged, wrong-item and quality refunds, across all of their Cartwise Grocery Orders orders and dated within the rolling 90 calendar days ending today, are counted; the new refund may be booked only while that count is *below* the service level's rolling refund-count limit. A count equal to the limit already fails the test.
- **Amount test.** The same refunds' total in that window, together with the amount now asked, may not *exceed* the rolling refund-amount limit. A total that lands exactly on the limit still passes.
- **Which limits.** Both limits are those of the service level of the order the new issue concerns.
- **Timing of the test.** While a line of the order is billed although recorded as not found and its refund does not yet stand on the order, the claim is not weighed against the rolling limits.
- **Timing of registration.** While the part of a not-found line above its unfound-line room does not yet stand as a submitted over-cap review request, no limit-review claim is registered.

| Count test | Amount test | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Passes | Passes | The rolling limits do not stop the refund |
| Fails | either | Nothing booked; the whole issue becomes the customer's limit-review claim |
| Passes | Fails | Nothing booked; the whole issue becomes the customer's limit-review claim |

## Customer tool reference: `submit_limit_review_claim_079a4c96`

**What it does.** The customer submits, from their own Cartwise account, their claim on one item line of a grocery order to the refund review team, when the support desk cannot book that refund because the customer's recent refunds have reached the rolling limits. One call registers one review request for the named order line with the review type "rolling limit review", the requested amount and the status "submitted". Nothing is refunded by the call and the order's billed amount does not change. The customer sees the claim at once among the order's review requests, stamped with the current time, and it stays submitted until the review team approves or denies it.

**How it is invoked.** It is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`, naming `submit_limit_review_claim_079a4c96`, and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it from their own account.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The customer reference number of the claimant's own profile, handed over by the support agent from the customer profile lookup | Id |
| `order_id` | The order number of the grocery order the claim concerns, handed over by the support agent from the order lookup | Id |
| `line_number` | The position of the claimed item line on the order, exactly as shown on the billed line entry | Integer (1, 2, 3 ...), no decimals |
| `refund_reason` | The controlled reason of the claim | Exactly one of `missing` (the billed product never reached the customer), `damaged` (arrived broken, crushed or leaking), `wrong_item` (a different product from the one ordered or approved was handed over), `quality` (arrived spoiled, melted, expired or otherwise unfit) |
| `requested_amount_usd` | The amount the claim asks the review team for | USD, positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed; never 0 or negative |

**Return.** A receipt rendered as text with `order_review_request_id` (the reference number of the new claim), `order_id`, `line_number` (the line claimed), `refund_reason` (the reason claimed), `request_type` (always `refund_limit_review`), `requested_amount_usd` (USD with 2 decimal places) and `request_status` ("submitted" when the claim now waits for the review team).

## Contract points

- *Who runs the claim?* The customer themselves, from their own Cartwise account, once the agent has unlocked and handed over the tool.
- *Does a submitted claim refund anything?* No. It registers a review request only; the order's billed amount does not change.
- *Who decides the claim?* The review team.
